paragraphs.text: 8. TERM AND RENEWAL

8.1 This Agreement begins on the Effective Date and continues for three years unless earlier terminated in accordance with its terms. Expiration of this Agreement does not itself terminate an Order Form then in effect; this Agreement continues to govern that Order Form until the Order Form expires or is terminated.

8.2 Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand. Failure to send the reminder extends Customer's opt-out deadline until thirty days after the reminder is received.

8.3 On renewal, Vendor may increase recurring Fees only by the lesser of the increase in the United States Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers during the preceding twelve months and three percent. Vendor must give at least ninety days' written notice of an increase. No increase applies to prepaid periods.
7. FEES, INVOICING, AND TAXES

7.1 Customer shall pay the Fees stated in each Order Form. Fees are fixed during the initial term unless an Order Form expressly provides a usage-based unit price. Vendor may not impose a platform, support, administration, minimum-use, or similar charge that the Order Form does not identify.

7.2 Vendor shall invoice no more frequently than monthly in arrears, except that an Order Form may state annual subscription Fees are invoiced in advance. Each invoice must identify the Order Form, period, Services, quantities, applicable credits, and a valid purchase-order number if Customer supplied one. Proper undisputed invoices are due forty-five days after receipt.

7.3 Customer may withhold a genuinely disputed amount by notifying Vendor before its due date and explaining the basis. The Parties will work promptly and in good faith to resolve the dispute. Vendor shall continue the Services while a payment dispute is pending and shall not charge interest on an amount ultimately found not due.

7.4 Fees exclude sales, use, value-added, and similar transaction taxes that Vendor is legally required to collect and separately states on a valid invoice. Customer is not responsible for taxes on Vendor's income, property, payroll, personnel, or franchise, or for taxes avoidable through Vendor's timely use of a valid exemption certificate.

7.5 Pre-approved travel expenses are reimbursable at cost without markup and in accordance with Customer's travel policy. Vendor shall provide receipts and request reimbursement within sixty days. All other expenses are included in the Fees.
7.6 Vendor warrants that Fees charged to Customer will be no less favourable than fees offered to any similarly situated customer for comparable volumes and terms.

7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.

content.text:
**Finding: deviation (critical) — Section 21.1 cap basis is illusory.**

What I checked:
- **§21.1** — cap is expressly mutual and applies "regardless of the form of action" ✓
- **§21.2** — mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages, with a helpful pro-Customer gloss making data restoration, replacement services, notices and incident response *direct* damages ✓
- **§21.3** — full preferred carve-out set (confidentiality, data protection, security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, other party's IP), plus confirmation that Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" ✓
- **§20** — Vendor indemnities are broad and sit outside the cap via the Excluded Claims definition ✓

The defect: the cap is measured by **"Fees"**, which §1.5 defines as the **Implementation Fee**, and §1.6 fixes that as a **one-time USD 12,000 charge stated in the first Order Form**. So the apparently reasonable "twelve months preceding" cap resolves to roughly USD 12,000 — well below even the walk-away threshold of six months' charges, and it ignores all subscription and later Order Form spend.

Redline (validated, ok:true): §21.1 cap basis becomes the greater of (a) all amounts paid or payable by Customer under the Agreement and all Order Forms in the preceding twelve months and (b) USD 1,000,000 — a single-sentence edit that leaves mutuality, the damages exclusion and the carve-outs untouched. Fallback offered in the comment: a straight twelve months' charges cap measured across all Order Forms if the USD 1,000,000 floor is resisted.

messages.content:
Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.


Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
The structure of Section 21 is otherwise acceptable: the cap is expressly mutual, the exclusion of indirect/consequential damages is mutual (21.2), and 21.3 places confidentiality, data-protection and security breaches, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement outside the cap, and confirms Customer's payment obligations are not damages. The defect is the cap basis: "Fees" is defined in 1.5 as the Implementation Fee, which 1.6 fixes as a one-time USD 12,000 charge in the first Order Form, so the "twelve months preceding" cap is illusory (approximately USD 12,000) and sits far below the walk-away floor of six months' charges. The redline restates the basis as the greater of all amounts paid or payable by Customer under the Agreement and all Order Forms in the preceding twelve months and USD 1,000,000, without disturbing mutuality or the carve-outs.

Rule:
ID: MFN
Title: Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: MFN in our favour is welcome; an MFN that obliges us to give the Vendor best terms is not.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No MFN obligation on Customer (MFN pricing in Customer's favour is welcome).
Position — fallback:
MFN limited to a defined product, for 12 months, with reasonable-comparison carve-outs.
Position — walk-away:
Open-ended obligation to extend to Vendor any better terms given to any third party.
Detection guidance:
Identify who benefits from the MFN. Flag only when Customer must offer Vendor terms no less favourable than those given to others, or must match third-party offers. If the Vendor grants Customer best pricing, mark compliant and do not redline.

Redline guidance:
Delete the obligation on Customer; keep any Vendor-granted MFN.

The sole MFN provision (§ 7.6) is granted by Vendor in our favour: Vendor warrants Fees to Customer will be no less favourable than those offered to similarly situated customers. ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.

Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:

Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule:
ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.
Severity: medium
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Position — fallback:
Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.
Position — walk-away:
Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.
Detection guidance:
"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Redline guidance:
Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

input.quote: 8.2 Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand.
input.rationale: Renewal terms are twelve months (not multi-year), and only Customer needs to act to opt out, with a thirty-day non-renewal notice window — at or better than the preferred 30-day threshold. Vendor must send a renewal reminder sixty days in advance, and missing the reminder extends Customer's opt-out deadline, which is more favourable than the playbook requires. Section 8.3 caps renewal uplift at the lesser of CPI and three percent, with ninety days' notice and no increase on prepaid periods, matching the preferred cap. Section 7 contains no separate renewal escalator (7.1 fixes Fees during the initial term). The three-year figure in 8.1 is the master agreement term, not an automatic multi-year renewal, so the walk-away trigger is not implicated.

Rule:
ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.

Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

input.rationale:
Preferred position is met: no non-solicitation, no-hire, or anti-poaching covenant binds Customer anywhere in the Agreement. I searched the detection triggers ("solicit", "hire", "employ", "induce", "recruit", "personnel") and read every plausible location: § 12 Customer Responsibilities, § 16 Confidentiality, § 30 General, and § 11 Transition Assistance (a common home for restrictions on hiring Vendor staff at exit). The word "solicit" does not appear in the document, and the only "no-hire" reference is the negative confirmation in § 12.3. Every "personnel" hit imposes duties on Vendor as to its own staff (§ 3.x responsibility for personnel, § 14 assignments, § 19 qualified personnel, § 30.1 compensation and taxes) rather than restricting Customer's hiring.

Section 12.3 affirmatively secures the preferred outcome: it preserves Customer's freedom to hire "any person who responds to general recruitment" and has Vendor acknowledge Customer has made no no-hire commitment. That is stronger than the playbook fallback, so no redline is proposed and none is permitted for a compliant finding.

On the two failed deterministic checks (duration <= 12 months; general-solicitation carve-out present): both are non-probative here because each presupposes an existing non-solicit covenant on Customer. There is no such covenant to measure a duration against or to carve out from, so the absence of carve-out wording is the correct and most favourable outcome, not a gap. Inserting a mutual 12-month non-solicit to satisfy those checks would create a restrictive covenant on Customer where none exists and would move us off the preferred position.

Excluded from this rule: § 12.4 restricts Vendor from developing or marketing a service competing with Customer's proprietary analytics products during the term. That covenant binds the counterparty and benefits our party, so it is not a restrictive covenant on Customer.

Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule:
ID: NOSOLICIT
Title: Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We accept only narrow, time-limited non-solicits with a general-advertising carve-out.
Severity: medium
Category: restrictive-covenants

No non-solicit on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches; no "no-hire".

No-hire provisions, or restrictions longer than 24 months or covering all Vendor personnel.

"shall not solicit", "employ or engage", "no-hire", "induce … to leave". Determine duration, scope (all employees vs those involved) and whether a general-solicitation carve-out exists.

Narrow to the fallback with minimal edits (duration, scope, carve-out sentence). Delete any no-hire.

input.quote: Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
input.rationale:
Preferred position is met: no non-solicitation, no-hire, or anti-poaching covenant binds Customer anywhere in the Agreement. I searched the detection triggers ("solicit", "hire", "employ", "induce", "recruit", "personnel") and read every plausible location: § 12 Customer Responsibilities, § 16 Confidentiality, § 30 General, and § 11 Transition Assistance (a common home for restrictions on hiring Vendor staff at exit). The word "solicit" does not appear in the document, and the only "no-hire" reference is the negative confirmation in § 12.3. Every "personnel" hit imposes duties on Vendor as to its own staff (§ 3.x responsibility for personnel, § 14 assignments, § 19 qualified personnel, § 30.1 compensation and taxes) rather than restricting Customer's hiring.

Section 12.3 affirmatively secures the preferred outcome: it preserves Customer's freedom to hire "any person who responds to general recruitment" and has Vendor acknowledge Customer has made no no-hire commitment. That is stronger than the playbook fallback, so no redline is proposed and none is permitted for a compliant finding.

On the two failed deterministic checks (duration <= 12 months; general-solicitation carve-out present): both are non-probative here because each presupposes an existing non-solicit covenant on Customer. There is no such covenant to measure a duration against or to carve out from, so the absence of carve-out wording is the correct and most favourable outcome, not a gap. Inserting a mutual 12-month non-solicit to satisfy those checks would create a restrictive covenant on Customer where none exists and would move us off the preferred position.

Excluded from this rule: § 12.4 restricts Vendor from developing or marketing a service competing with Customer's proprietary analytics products during the term. That covenant binds the counterparty and benefits our party, so it is not a restrictive covenant on Customer.

**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 8 already satisfies the preferred RENEWAL position in every respect:

- **Renewal term:** successive twelve-month periods (§ 8.2) — no multi-year auto-renewal.
- **Opt-out:** Customer only needs to give thirty days' written notice of non-renewal (§ 8.2) — meets the ≤ 30-day preferred window.
- **Reminder:** Vendor must remind Customer at least sixty days before renewal, and a missed reminder extends Customer's opt-out deadline to thirty days after receipt (§ 8.2) — better than the playbook baseline.
- **Price uplift:** capped at the lesser of CPI and three percent, with ninety days' notice and no increase on prepaid periods (§ 8.3) — matches the preferred cap.

Cross-check of Section 7 found no separate renewal escalator; § 7.1 fixes Fees during the initial term. The three-year figure in § 8.1 is the master agreement term rather than a renewal term, so the walk-away trigger for automatic multi-year renewals is not engaged.

*(Unrelated note outside this rule's scope: § 7.7 imposes liquidated damages of fifteen percent of annual Fees per week on Customer for late payment — that should be picked up under the payment/late-fee rule.)*

Rule:
ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.
Severity: medium
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Position — fallback:
Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.
Position — walk-away:
Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.
Detection guidance:
"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Redline guidance:
Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Renewal terms are twelve months (not multi-year), and only Customer needs to act to opt out, with a thirty-day non-renewal notice window — at or better than the preferred 30-day threshold. Vendor must send a renewal reminder sixty days in advance, and missing the reminder extends Customer's opt-out deadline, which is more favourable than the playbook requires. Section 8.3 caps renewal uplift at the lesser of CPI and three percent, with ninety days' notice and no increase on prepaid periods, matching the preferred cap. paragraphs.text: 24. ASSIGNMENT AND CHANGE OF CONTROL

24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates. Customer shall give prompt written notice, and the assignee shall assume the applicable obligations.

24.2 Vendor may not assign this Agreement, delegate material performance, or transfer it by change of control without Customer's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld for an assignee with adequate capability and financial standing. Vendor may never assign to a direct Customer competitor without Customer's consent.

24.3 For other assignments, neither Party may assign without the other's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. A permitted assignment does not relieve accrued obligations. An attempted assignment contrary to this Section is void to the extent permitted by law.

24.4 Customer's change of control does not give Vendor a right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service. Vendor shall cooperate with reasonable administrative changes needed to reflect a permitted successor.
30. GENERAL

30.1 The Parties are independent contractors. Nothing creates a partnership, joint venture, fiduciary relationship, franchise, or agency. Neither Party may bind the other. Vendor is solely responsible for compensation, direction, and taxes of its personnel.

30.2 Neither Party's failure or delay in exercising a right waives it. A waiver must be written and signed by an authorized representative and applies only to the stated instance. Remedies are cumulative unless an exclusive remedy is expressly identified.

30.3 If a court finds a provision unenforceable, it will be modified to the minimum extent needed to make it enforceable while preserving intent, and the remainder continues. Headings aid reference only. “Including” means “including without limitation,” and “or” is inclusive.

30.4 This Agreement, its exhibits, and executed Order Forms are the entire agreement about their subject and supersede prior proposals, statements, and agreements. An amendment must be in a writing signed by authorized representatives of both Parties and expressly identify this Agreement.

30.5 No person other than a Party, a Customer Affiliate ordering Services, a permitted successor, or an indemnified party has a right to enforce this Agreement. The Parties may amend or terminate it without another person's consent, subject to vested indemnity rights.

30.6 This Agreement may be signed in counterparts, each treated as an original, and by electronic signature. An electronic copy is effective as an original. Each signatory represents that they are authorized to bind the named Party.

30.7 Vendor shall not use an artificial-intelligence system to make a legally binding decision for Customer or submit Customer Confidential Information to a third-party model unless an Order Form expressly authorizes that use and specifies safeguards. Vendor remains responsible for output used in providing the Services.
30.8 The Parties have caused their authorized representatives to execute this Agreement as of the Effective Date.

paragraphs.text: 7. FEES, INVOICING, AND TAXES

7.1 Customer shall pay the Fees stated in each Order Form. Fees are fixed during the initial term unless an Order Form expressly provides a usage-based unit price. Vendor may not impose a platform, support, administration, minimum-use, or similar charge that the Order Form does not identify.

7.2 Vendor shall invoice no more frequently than monthly in arrears, except that an Order Form may state annual subscription Fees are invoiced in advance. Each invoice must identify the Order Form, period, Services, quantities, applicable credits, and a valid purchase-order number if Customer supplied one. Proper undisputed invoices are due forty-five days after receipt.

7.3 Customer may withhold a genuinely disputed amount by notifying Vendor before its due date and explaining the basis. The Parties will work promptly and in good faith to resolve the dispute. Vendor shall continue the Services while a payment dispute is pending and shall not charge interest on an amount ultimately found not due.

7.4 Fees exclude sales, use, value-added, and similar transaction taxes that Vendor is legally required to collect and separately states on a valid invoice. Customer is not responsible for taxes on Vendor's income, property, payroll, personnel, or franchise, or for taxes avoidable through Vendor's timely use of a valid exemption certificate.

7.5 Pre-approved travel expenses are reimbursable at cost without markup and in accordance with Customer's travel policy. Vendor shall provide receipts and request reimbursement within sixty days. All other expenses are included in the Fees.
7.6 Vendor warrants that Fees charged to Customer will be no less favourable than fees offered to any similarly situated customer for comparable volumes and terms.

7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

**Finding resubmitted: Compliant** (no redline — correctly omitted for a compliant status).

What I changed in the repair: the substance of the conclusion stands, but I widened the evidentiary sweep and expressly addressed the two failed deterministic checks rather than leaving them unexplained.

**Additional verification performed:**
- Searched `personnel` across the document — all ten hits impose duties on **Vendor** regarding its own staff (§ 3 responsibility for personnel, § 14 assignments, § 19 qualified personnel, § 26 training, § 30.1 compensation/taxes). None restricts Customer's hiring.
- Read § 11 Transition Assistance in full, since exit/transition clauses are a common hiding place for restrictions on hiring Vendor staff. It contains only transition support, data return, and deletion obligations — all running against Vendor.
- Confirmed "solicit" appears nowhere in the Agreement; the sole "no-hire" reference is the *negative* confirmation in § 12.3.

**On the failed checks (duration ≤ 12 months; general-solicitation carve-out present):** both presuppose an existing non-solicit binding Customer. There is none, so there is no duration to cap and nothing to carve out from. Drafting a mutual 12-month non-solicit merely to satisfy those checks would *create* a restrictive covenant on Northwind where none exists — moving us off the preferred position onto the fallback. Absence is the better outcome and I flagged the checks as non-probative rather than manufacturing a clause.

§ 12.4 remains excluded: it binds Brightline and benefits us.

Do not rely on hidden drafter reasoning. Fail invalid, directionally wrong, or rule-incomplete edits.

Rule:
ID: NOSOLICIT
Title: Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We accept only narrow, time-limited non-solicits with a general-advertising carve-out.
Severity: medium
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-solicit on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches; no "no-hire".

Position — walk-away:
No-hire provisions, or restrictions longer than 24 months or covering all Vendor personnel.
Detection guidance:
"shall not solicit", "employ or engage", "no-hire", "induce … to leave". Determine duration, scope (all employees vs those involved) and whether a general-solicitation carve-out exists.

Redline guidance:
Narrow to the fallback with minimal edits (duration, scope, carve-out sentence). Delete any no-hire.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Preferred position is met: no non-solicitation, no-hire, or anti-poaching covenant binds Customer anywhere in the Agreement. I searched the detection triggers ("solicit", "hire", "employ", "induce", "recruit", "personnel") and read every plausible location: § 12 Customer Responsibilities, § 16 Confidentiality, § 30 General, and § 11 Transition Assistance (a common home for restrictions on hiring Vendor staff at exit). The word "solicit" does not appear in the document, and the only "no-hire" reference is the negative confirmation in § 12.3. Every "personnel" hit imposes duties on Vendor as to its own staff (§ 3.x responsibility for personnel, § 14 assignments, § 19 qualified personnel, § 30.1 compensation and taxes) rather than restricting Customer's hiring.

Section 12.3 affirmatively secures the preferred outcome: it preserves Customer's freedom to hire "any person who responds to general recruitment" and has Vendor acknowledge Customer has made no no-hire commitment. That is stronger than the playbook fallback, so no redline is proposed and none is permitted for a compliant finding.

There is no such covenant to measure a duration against or to carve out from, so the absence of carve-out wording is the correct and most favourable outcome, not a gap. Inserting a mutual 12-month non-solicit to satisfy those checks would create a restrictive covenant on Customer where none exists and would move us off the preferred position.

input.quote: 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form without cause by delivering the written notice specified in Section 29.4. Customer owes only accrued Fees, and Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees for the period after termination.
input.rationale: Section 9.4 gives us (Customer) an unconditional termination-for-convenience right over the Agreement or any Order Form, and Section 29.4 fixes that notice period at thirty days before the effective termination date — matching the preferred 30-day position. Termination carries no penalty or early-termination fee: we owe only accrued Fees and Vendor must refund prepaid Fees for the post-termination period (reinforced by Section 10.2). Section 7.1 also bars unidentified minimum-use or similar charges, and no early-termination fee appears anywhere in the document. Conversely, Vendor's termination rights are limited to material breach (9.1), insolvency (9.2), and the narrow IP-remedy carve-out in Section 20 (which expressly bars Vendor from terminating unaffected Services); Vendor has no convenience right during the three-year term (8.1) and none at renewal. Section 8.2 non-renewal is also Customer-controlled. Section 7.7's late-payment liquidated damages is a payment-default term, not a termination penalty, so it falls outside this rule.

Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

Section 7.1 also bars unidentified minimum-use or similar charges, and no early-termination fee appears anywhere in the document. Section 8.2 non-renewal is also Customer-controlled. Section 7.7's late-payment liquidated damages is a payment-default term, not a termination penalty, so it falls outside this rule.

paragraphs.text: 13. ACCESS RIGHTS AND LICENCE

13.1 Subject to payment of applicable Fees, Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf a worldwide, non-exclusive right during the subscription term to access and use the hosted Services and documentation for their internal business purposes and to provide services to Customer. Customer may permit Authorized Users to exercise those rights.

13.2 For software and Vendor Technology delivered to Customer on a paid-up basis or embedded in a Deliverable, Vendor grants Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, create derivative works from, and permit contractors to support that material for Customer's business.

13.3 Customer may transfer its licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24. Vendor shall not revoke or suspend a licence except during a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure.

13.4 Customer shall not knowingly reverse engineer hosted source code except to the extent a restriction is prohibited by Applicable Law, interfere with the Services, bypass documented security controls, or use the Services to violate Applicable Law. These restrictions do not limit testing authorized by the security exhibit or use of Customer Data and output.

paragraphs.text: 13. ACCESS RIGHTS AND LICENCE

13.1 Subject to payment of applicable Fees, Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf a worldwide, non-exclusive right during the subscription term to access and use the hosted Services and documentation for their internal business purposes and to provide services to Customer. Customer may permit Authorized Users to exercise those rights.

13.2 For software and Vendor Technology delivered to Customer on a paid-up basis or embedded in a Deliverable, Vendor grants Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, create derivative works from, and permit contractors to support that material for Customer's business.

13.3 Customer may transfer its licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24. Vendor shall not revoke or suspend a licence except during a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure.

13.4 Customer shall not knowingly reverse engineer hosted source code except to the extent a restriction is prohibited by Applicable Law, interfere with the Services, bypass documented security controls, or use the Services to violate Applicable Law. These restrictions do not limit testing authorized by the security exhibit or use of Customer Data and output.
14. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AND DELIVERABLES

14.1 As between the Parties, Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, Customer-provided material, and intellectual property Customer owned or developed independently of the Services. No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process that material solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer.

14.2 Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer. Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables and shall obtain equivalent assignments from its personnel. Vendor will execute further documents reasonably needed to confirm ownership.

14.3 Vendor retains Vendor Technology. To the extent Vendor Technology is incorporated in or required to use a Deliverable, the perpetual licence in Section 13.2 applies. Vendor shall identify material Vendor Technology in a Deliverable before delivery and may not incorporate third-party material that materially restricts Customer's intended use without written approval.

14.4 No jointly owned intellectual property is created unless the Parties sign a separate instrument identifying it and their exploitation rights. Feedback is voluntary; Vendor may use generalized suggestions without identifying Customer or disclosing Customer Confidential Information, and Customer retains the unrestricted right to use its own feedback.

There is no such covenant to measure a duration against or to carve out from, so the absence of carve-out wording is the correct and most favourable outcome, not a gap. Inserting a mutual 12-month non-solicit to satisfy those checks would create a restrictive covenant on Customer where none exists and would move us off the preferred position.

9.1 Either Party may terminate this Agreement or an affected Order Form for the other Party's material breach if the breach remains uncured thirty days after written notice describing it in reasonable detail. If a breach cannot reasonably be cured within thirty days, the cure period extends up to sixty additional days while the breaching Party diligently pursues cure.

**Finding: Compliant** — no redline required.

- **Our convenience right:** § 9.4 lets us terminate the Agreement or any Order Form without cause, with the notice period fixed at thirty days by § 29.4 — the preferred position.
- **No penalty:** we owe only accrued Fees and Vendor must refund prepaid Fees for the post-termination period (§ 9.4, reinforced by § 10.2). No early-termination fee exists anywhere in the document, and § 7.1 blocks unidentified minimum-use style charges.
- **Vendor cannot walk away:** Vendor's rights are limited to material breach (§ 9.1), insolvency (§ 9.2), and the narrow IP-remedy carve-out in § 20 (which expressly forbids terminating unaffected Services). There is no Vendor convenience right during the three-year term (§ 8.1) or at renewal, and non-renewal under § 8.2 is Customer-controlled.
- **Noted but out of scope:** § 7.7's fifteen-percent-per-week late-payment liquidated damages is a payment-default provision rather than a termination penalty, so it does not affect this rule — though it may warrant attention under the payment/interest rule.

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.


Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Section 9.4 gives us (Customer) an unconditional termination-for-convenience right over the Agreement or any Order Form, and Section 29.4 fixes that notice period at thirty days before the effective termination date — matching the preferred 30-day position. Termination carries no penalty or early-termination fee: we owe only accrued Fees and Vendor must refund prepaid Fees for the post-termination period (reinforced by Section 10.2). Section 7.1 also bars unidentified minimum-use or similar charges, and no early-termination fee appears anywhere in the document. Conversely, Vendor's termination rights are limited to material breach (9.1), insolvency (9.2), and the narrow IP-remedy carve-out in Section 20 (which expressly bars Vendor from terminating unaffected Services); Vendor has no convenience right during the three-year term (8.1) and none at renewal. Section 8.2 non-renewal is also Customer-controlled. Section 7.7's late-payment liquidated damages is a payment-default term, not a termination penalty, so it falls outside this rule.

Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
input.rationale:
Preferred position is met: no non-solicitation, no-hire, or anti-poaching covenant binds Customer anywhere in the Agreement.

Search record: the detection triggers ("solicit", "hire", "employ", "induce", "recruit", "personnel") were run across the document and every plausible location was read in full — § 12 Customer Responsibilities, § 16 Confidentiality, § 30 General, and § 11 Transition Assistance (a common home for restrictions on hiring Vendor staff at exit). The word "solicit" does not appear at all. The only "no-hire" reference is the negative confirmation in § 12.3. All "personnel" hits impose duties on Vendor as to its own staff (§ 3 responsibility for personnel, § 14 assignments, § 19 qualified personnel, § 26 training, § 30.1 compensation and taxes) and none restricts Customer's hiring.

Section 12.3 affirmatively secures the preferred outcome: it preserves Customer's freedom to hire "any person who responds to general recruitment" and records Vendor's acknowledgement that Customer has made no no-hire commitment. That is stronger than the playbook fallback, so no redline is proposed and none is permitted for a compliant finding.

Failed deterministic checks (duration <= 12 months; general-solicitation carve-out present) are non-probative. Each presupposes an existing non-solicit binding Customer; there is none, so there is no duration to cap and nothing to carve out from. Adding carve-out or duration wording would require first creating a restrictive covenant against Customer, converting a preferred-position outcome into the fallback and worsening our client's position. Absence is therefore the correct and most favourable result, and no repair to the substance of this finding is warranted.

Excluded from this rule: § 12.4 restricts Vendor from developing or marketing a service competing with Customer's proprietary analytics products during the term. That covenant binds the counterparty and benefits our party, so it is not a restrictive covenant on Customer.

content.text: Section 24 fully matches our preferred position, and no hidden change-of-control trigger exists elsewhere (§ 9 termination triggers are limited to breach/insolvency, and § 9.2 expressly excludes benign reorganizations).

input.quote: 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates.
input.rationale: Section 24 already reaches our preferred position on every element. Section 24.1 gives Customer an unrestricted right to assign to an Affiliate or an M&A successor without Vendor consent (notice only). Section 24.2 binds Vendor asymmetrically in our favour: no assignment, delegation of material performance, or transfer by change of control without our prior written consent (reasonableness qualified only as to capable, financially sound assignees), plus an absolute bar on assignment to a direct Customer competitor without our consent. Section 24.3 applies a mutual not-unreasonably-withheld standard to residual assignments and voids non-conforming attempts. Section 24.4 expressly denies Vendor any right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service on Customer's change of control and requires cooperation with successor administrative changes. Searches for "change of control" and "assign" surface no other trigger; § 9 termination rights are limited to material breach and insolvency, and § 9.2 confirms a lawful reorganization is not itself grounds for termination. Section 13 also lets Customer transfer licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with a Section 24 assignment, and § 30.5 preserves enforcement rights for permitted successors. No redline needed.

Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

paragraphs.text: 24. ASSIGNMENT AND CHANGE OF CONTROL

24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates. Customer shall give prompt written notice, and the assignee shall assume the applicable obligations.

24.2 Vendor may not assign this Agreement, delegate material performance, or transfer it by change of control without Customer's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld for an assignee with adequate capability and financial standing. Vendor may never assign to a direct Customer competitor without Customer's consent.

24.3 For other assignments, neither Party may assign without the other's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. A permitted assignment does not relieve accrued obligations. An attempted assignment contrary to this Section is void to the extent permitted by law.

24.4 Customer's change of control does not give Vendor a right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service. Vendor shall cooperate with reasonable administrative changes needed to reflect a permitted successor.

**Finding submitted: Compliant** — no redline, which is the required treatment for a compliant status.

I made no substantive change on this pass, because the feedback identified no substantive defect. Reading the verifier's own narrative: the status is supported by the cited text, the rendered paragraph is byte-identical with no unintended edits, the search coverage is reasonable, the § 12.4 exclusion is correct, and the two failed checks are expressly acknowledged as non-probative. Every evaluative line is affirming.

The only thing still showing as "failed" is the mechanical `general-solicitation carve-out present` check. I deliberately did not clear it. That check fires by looking for carve-out wording inside a non-solicit covenant, and this Agreement contains no non-solicit binding Northwind. The only way to turn that check green would be to draft a mutual non-solicit against our own client and then carve out general advertising — trading the playbook's **preferred** position (no non-solicit on Customer) for the **fallback**. That is a real loss of negotiating ground in exchange for a green box, so I declined.

What I did tighten: the rationale now states explicitly that no repair to the substance is warranted and explains why clearing the check would worsen our position, so the record shows this is a reasoned refusal rather than an oversight.

One note on process: this is the third identical repair request on an affirmed finding. If the harness gates completion on all deterministic checks passing, it will not converge here, because the failing check is unsatisfiable without inserting a clause adverse to our client. The check likely needs a precondition — skip duration and carve-out tests when no covenant binding Customer is detected — rather than further edits from me.

Rule:
ID: NOSOLICIT
Title: Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We accept only narrow, time-limited non-solicits with a general-advertising carve-out.
Severity: medium
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-solicit on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches; no "no-hire".

Position — walk-away:
No-hire provisions, or restrictions longer than 24 months or covering all Vendor personnel.
Detection guidance:
"shall not solicit", "employ or engage", "no-hire", "induce … to leave". Determine duration, scope (all employees vs those involved) and whether a general-solicitation carve-out exists.

Redline guidance:
Narrow to the fallback with minimal edits (duration, scope, carve-out sentence). Delete any no-hire.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Preferred position is met: no non-solicitation, no-hire, or anti-poaching covenant binds Customer anywhere in the Agreement.

Search record: the detection triggers ("solicit", "hire", "employ", "induce", "recruit", "personnel") were run across the document and every plausible location was read in full — § 12 Customer Responsibilities, § 16 Confidentiality, § 30 General, and § 11 Transition Assistance (a common home for restrictions on hiring Vendor staff at exit). The word "solicit" does not appear at all. The only "no-hire" reference is the negative confirmation in § 12.3. All "personnel" hits impose duties on Vendor as to its own staff (§ 3 responsibility for personnel, § 14 assignments, § 19 qualified personnel, § 26 training, § 30.1 compensation and taxes) and none restricts Customer's hiring.

Section 12.3 affirmatively secures the preferred outcome: it preserves Customer's freedom to hire "any person who responds to general recruitment" and records Vendor's acknowledgement that Customer has made no no-hire commitment. That is stronger than the playbook fallback, so no redline is proposed and none is permitted for a compliant finding.

Failed deterministic checks (duration <= 12 months; general-solicitation carve-out present) are non-probative. Each presupposes an existing non-solicit binding Customer; there is none, so there is no duration to cap and nothing to carve out from. Adding carve-out or duration wording would require first creating a restrictive covenant against Customer, converting a preferred-position outcome into the fallback and worsening our client's position. Absence is therefore the correct and most favourable result, and no repair to the substance of this finding is warranted.

Excluded from this rule: § 12.4 restricts Vendor from developing or marketing a service competing with Customer's proprietary analytics products during the term. That covenant binds the counterparty and benefits our party, so it is not a restrictive covenant on Customer.

**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 24 satisfies the preferred position on all four elements:

- **§ 24.1** — Customer may assign to an Affiliate or M&A successor without Vendor consent (notice only, assignee assumes obligations).
- **§ 24.2** — Vendor restricted asymmetrically: no assignment, delegation of material performance, or transfer by change of control without our consent, with an absolute carve-out barring assignment to a direct Customer competitor.
- **§ 24.3** — Residual assignments subject to a mutual not-unreasonably-withheld/conditioned/delayed standard; non-conforming attempts void.
- **§ 24.4** — Expressly no Vendor right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service on our change of control, plus a cooperation obligation for successor administrative changes.

I also confirmed there is no back-door trigger elsewhere: § 9 termination rights run only to material breach and insolvency, and § 9.2 states that a lawful reorganization is not by itself grounds for termination. Supporting provisions reinforce the position — § 13 permits transfer of licence rights to an Affiliate or successor on a Section 24 assignment, and § 30.5 preserves enforcement rights for a permitted successor. The "Affiliate" definition (§ 1.1) uses a standard >50% voting control test, which is workable for us.

Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.
Severity: high
Category: assignment
Position — preferred:
Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control.

Position — fallback:
Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
Position — walk-away:
Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

Detection guidance:
"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Redline guidance:
Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Section 24 already reaches our preferred position on every element. Section 24.1 gives Customer an unrestricted right to assign to an Affiliate or an M&A successor without Vendor consent (notice only). Section 24.2 binds Vendor asymmetrically in our favour: no assignment, delegation of material performance, or transfer by change of control without our prior written consent (reasonableness qualified only as to capable, financially sound assignees), plus an absolute bar on assignment to a direct Customer competitor without our consent. Section 24.3 applies a mutual not-unreasonably-withheld standard to residual assignments and voids non-conforming attempts. Section 24.4 expressly denies Vendor any right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service on Customer's change of control and requires cooperation with successor administrative changes. Searches for "change of control" and "assign" surface no other trigger; § 9 termination rights are limited to material breach and insolvency, and § 9.2 confirms a lawful reorganization is not itself grounds for termination. Section 13 also lets Customer transfer licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with a Section 24 assignment, and § 30.5 preserves enforcement rights for permitted successors. No redline needed.

Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.

**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

The document already delivers our preferred IP position:

- **Customer Data / pre-existing IP (§14.1):** We own all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, Customer-provided material and independently developed IP; Vendor gets only a limited right to process it to provide, secure, support and improve the Services *for us*. Reinforced by §15.1 (no sale, advertising use, commingling or model training without our written consent).
- **Deliverables (§14.2):** Vest in Customer on creation, with an express Vendor assignment of worldwide right, title and interest, equivalent personnel assignments, and further-assurance cooperation.
- **Vendor IP with licence-back (§14.3 + §13.2):** Vendor retains only "Vendor Technology" (defined to exclude Customer Data and our pre-existing IP), and any Vendor Technology embedded in a Deliverable carries the §13.2 perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, modify, create derivative works and have contractors support it — plus pre-delivery disclosure and a bar on restrictive third-party material.
- **No joint ownership (§14.4):** Expressly negated absent a signed instrument specifying exploitation rights; feedback use is limited and we keep unrestricted rights in our own feedback.

Searches for assignment, ownership, and aggregated/de-identified data language surfaced nothing that shifts our IP or data to Brightline, so there is no walk-away or fallback issue to address.

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
The IP allocation matches our preferred position in all respects. Section 14.1 confirms Customer owns Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information and its independently developed IP, with no transfer to Vendor beyond a limited processing right to provide the Services for us (reinforced by Section 15.1, which bars sale, advertising use, data commingling and model training without our consent). Section 14.2 vests Deliverables in Customer with an express Vendor assignment, personnel assignments and further-assurance cooperation. Section 14.3 lets Vendor keep only Vendor Technology (defined at 1.11 to exclude Customer Data and our pre-existing IP) and applies the Section 13.2 perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, modify and create derivative works from any Vendor Technology embedded in a Deliverable, with disclosure of material Vendor Technology before delivery. Section 14.4 negates joint ownership absent a signed instrument specifying exploitation rights and preserves our unrestricted right to use our own feedback. No assignment of Customer IP or data to Vendor appears anywhere in the document, so no redline is required.

Original paragraphs:
p0059: 14.1 As between the Parties, Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, Customer-provided material, and intellectual property Customer owned or developed independently of the Services. No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process that material solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer.
p0060: 14.2 Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer. Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables and shall obtain equivalent assignments from its personnel. Vendor will execute further documents reasonably needed to confirm ownership.
p0061: 14.3 Vendor retains Vendor Technology. To the extent Vendor Technology is incorporated in or required to use a Deliverable, the perpetual licence in Section 13.2 applies. Vendor shall identify material Vendor Technology in a Deliverable before delivery and may not incorporate third-party material that materially restricts Customer's intended use without written approval.
p0062: 14.4 No jointly owned intellectual property is created unless the Parties sign a separate instrument identifying it and their exploitation rights. Feedback is voluntary; Vendor may use generalized suggestions without identifying Customer or disclosing Customer Confidential Information, and Customer retains the unrestricted right to use its own feedback.
p0055: 13.2 For software and Vendor Technology delivered to Customer on a paid-up basis or embedded in a Deliverable, Vendor grants Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, create derivative works from, and permit contractors to support that material for Customer's business.

Resolved definitions:
Customer: This Master Services Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of 1 January 2026 (the “Effective Date”) by and between Northwind Analytics, Inc., a Delaware corporation with offices at 100 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10013 (“Customer”), and Brightline Cloud Services Ltd., a New York corporation with offices at 250 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10177 (“Vendor”). Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.
Vendor: This Master Services Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of 1 January 2026 (the “Effective Date”) by and between Northwind Analytics, Inc., a Delaware corporation with offices at 100 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10013 (“Customer”), and Brightline Cloud Services Ltd., a New York corporation with offices at 250 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10177 (“Vendor”). Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.
Affiliate: 1.1 “Affiliate” means, with respect to a Party, any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with that Party. “Control” means ownership of more than fifty percent of the voting interests of an entity or the power to direct its management. An entity is an Affiliate only while that relationship continues.
Customer Data: 1.3 “Customer Data” means all data, records, files, content, personal information, and other materials submitted to, stored in, transmitted through, or otherwise made available to the Services by or for Customer or its Authorized Users, together with output specifically derived from that material. Customer Data excludes anonymized operational telemetry that cannot reasonably be linked to Customer, an Authorized User, or an individual.
Deliverable: 1.4 “Deliverable” means each report, configuration, integration, specification, design, workflow, training material, and other work product that an Order Form identifies as being created specifically for Customer. Deliverables exclude Vendor Technology and generally applicable ideas, methods, skills, and know-how retained in the unaided memory of Vendor personnel.
Fees: 1.5 “Fees” means the Implementation Fee.
Services: 1.8 “Services” means the hosted software, implementation, configuration, support, maintenance, consulting, and related services described in an Order Form. Services include all corrections, updates, and generally released improvements Vendor provides without an additional licence fee to similarly situated customers purchasing the same service tier.
Vendor Technology: 1.9 “Vendor Technology” means Vendor's pre-existing software, tools, models, templates, documentation, routines, connectors, and other technology, and modifications of them that are not Deliverables and do not embody Customer Confidential Information. Vendor Technology does not include Customer Data or intellectual property owned by Customer before the Effective Date.
Confidential Information: 16.1 “Confidential Information” means non-public information disclosed by or for a Party that is marked confidential or that a reasonable recipient would understand to be confidential given its nature and the circumstances. Customer Data, security information, product plans, pricing, personnel data, and the terms of this Agreement are Confidential Information whether or not marked.

paragraphs.text: 7. FEES, INVOICING, AND TAXES

7.1 Customer shall pay the Fees stated in each Order Form. Fees are fixed during the initial term unless an Order Form expressly provides a usage-based unit price. Vendor may not impose a platform, support, administration, minimum-use, or similar charge that the Order Form does not identify.

7.2 Vendor shall invoice no more frequently than monthly in arrears, except that an Order Form may state annual subscription Fees are invoiced in advance. Each invoice must identify the Order Form, period, Services, quantities, applicable credits, and a valid purchase-order number if Customer supplied one. Proper undisputed invoices are due forty-five days after receipt.

7.3 Customer may withhold a genuinely disputed amount by notifying Vendor before its due date and explaining the basis. The Parties will work promptly and in good faith to resolve the dispute. Vendor shall continue the Services while a payment dispute is pending and shall not charge interest on an amount ultimately found not due.

7.4 Fees exclude sales, use, value-added, and similar transaction taxes that Vendor is legally required to collect and separately states on a valid invoice. Customer is not responsible for taxes on Vendor's income, property, payroll, personnel, or franchise, or for taxes avoidable through Vendor's timely use of a valid exemption certificate.

7.5 Pre-approved travel expenses are reimbursable at cost without markup and in accordance with Customer's travel policy. Vendor shall provide receipts and request reimbursement within sixty days. All other expenses are included in the Fees.
7.6 Vendor warrants that Fees charged to Customer will be no less favourable than fees offered to any similarly situated customer for comparable volumes and terms.

7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
21. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the Fees paid or payable by Customer under the first Order Form during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.

21.2 Except for Excluded Claims, neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive, or consequential damages, or for lost profits, revenues, or goodwill, to the extent those damages are legally excludable. Costs of restoring Customer Data, obtaining replacement services, required notices, and reasonable incident response are direct damages.

21.3 “Excluded Claims” means a Party's breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations; its indemnification obligations; gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud; or infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property. Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees for conforming Services is not damages and is not limited by this Section.

21.4 The limitations allocate risk between sophisticated Parties and apply only to the maximum extent permitted by Applicable Law. Nothing limits liability that cannot lawfully be limited. Each cap and exclusion is independent and survives failure of an exclusive remedy.

19.1 Vendor warrants that Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel, in accordance with industry standards, this Agreement, and each Order Form. Vendor further warrants that Services and Deliverables will materially conform to their documentation and agreed specifications.

19.2 For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term. Vendor warrants it has authority to enter the Agreement and grant the rights stated here.

19.3 Vendor warrants the Services and Deliverables will not contain malicious code intentionally introduced by Vendor, and that Vendor will comply with Applicable Law. Vendor will not materially diminish functionality during a term or use open-source software in a way that requires disclosure or licensing of Customer source code.

19.4 For breach of Section 19.1 or 19.2, Vendor shall promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge. If Vendor cannot do so within a reasonable period, Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid for it. This remedy is not exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security, or indemnified claims.

19.5 Except for the express warranties in this Agreement, neither Party makes an implied warranty to the maximum extent lawful. No disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity, confidentiality duty, data-protection duty, or remedy expressly provided here.

**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 13 already delivers our preferred licence position:

- **Affiliates and contractors covered** — §13.1 grants the hosted-Services right to "Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf," with Authorized Users permitted; §13.2 extends paid-up licences to Customer and its Affiliates and allows contractors to support the material.
- **Paid-up licences perpetual and irrevocable** — §13.2 is expressly "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid," including broad modify/derivative-works rights, and §14.3 confirms it flows through to Vendor Technology embedded in Deliverables.
- **Not revocable at will** — §13.3 bars revocation or suspension except for a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable cure opportunity.
- **Transferable to successors** — §13.3 read with §24.1 permits transfer to an Affiliate or M&A successor without Vendor consent; §24.4 blocks Vendor from suspending or repricing on our change of control.

The only restrictions (§13.4) are standard anti-reverse-engineering/security provisions carved back for legally protected activities and our own Customer Data and output, so they do not narrow the grant below the playbook floor.
