Rule:
ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Position — fallback:
Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
Position — walk-away:
Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.
Detection guidance:
Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Section 13 satisfies the preferred position in full. §13.1 grants the subscription access right to Customer, its Affiliates and contractors acting on their behalf (plus Authorized Users), so no affiliate/contractor gap exists. §13.2 makes paid-up software and embedded Vendor Technology licences perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free and fully paid for Customer and its Affiliates, with contractor support permitted. §13.3 permits transfer to an Affiliate or successor under the broad Customer assignment right in §24.1 (merger, acquisition, sale of assets, no Vendor consent) and limits revocation or suspension to a material uncured payment or use breach after notice and a reasonable cure opportunity, so the grant is not revocable at will or unilaterally suspendable. §24.4 further bars Vendor from suspending or repricing on a Customer change of control. No redline needed.

Original paragraphs:
p0054: 13.1 Subject to payment of applicable Fees, Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf a worldwide, non-exclusive right during the subscription term to access and use the hosted Services and documentation for their internal business purposes and to provide services to Customer. Customer may permit Authorized Users to exercise those rights.
p0055: 13.2 For software and Vendor Technology delivered to Customer on a paid-up basis or embedded in a Deliverable, Vendor grants Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, create derivative works from, and permit contractors to support that material for Customer's business.
p0056: 13.3 Customer may transfer its licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24. Vendor shall not revoke or suspend a licence except during a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure.

6.1 Customer will have fifteen business days after delivery of a Deliverable to test it against the acceptance criteria in the applicable Order Form. Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

paragraphs.text: 9. TERMINATION

9.1 Either Party may terminate this Agreement or an affected Order Form for the other Party's material breach if the breach remains uncured thirty days after written notice describing it in reasonable detail. If a breach cannot reasonably be cured within thirty days, the cure period extends up to sixty additional days while the breaching Party diligently pursues cure.

9.2 Either Party may terminate immediately by written notice if the other becomes insolvent, makes a general assignment for creditors, enters liquidation, or becomes subject to a bankruptcy proceeding not dismissed within sixty days. A lawful reorganization that does not impair performance is not, by itself, grounds for termination.

9.3 Customer may terminate an Order Form immediately if Vendor suffers a material Security Incident, repeatedly misses a critical service level, violates Applicable Law in performing the Services, or infringes a third party's intellectual property and cannot provide the remedies required by Section 20.5.

9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form without cause by delivering the written notice specified in Section 29.4. Customer owes only accrued Fees, and Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees for the period after termination.

9.5 Termination of one Order Form does not terminate another Order Form unless Customer states that the affected Services are operationally inseparable. A termination right is in addition to, and does not exclude, any other remedy available under this Agreement or Applicable Law.

Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.

90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.

No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.

Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).

Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.

Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.

Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Section 22 is the only provision granting audit/verification rights against us (a document-wide search for audit, inspection, verification, monitoring, remote access and telemetry surfaced nothing else; § 23 contains only a heading). It matches the preferred position on every parameter: frequency limited to once in any twelve-month period, thirty days' prior written notice, normal business hours with no unreasonable disruption, off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality (§ 22.1); Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds five percent (§ 22.2); and Vendor and its auditor are expressly barred from direct access to Customer systems, unrelated Customer Data, privileged material and third-party confidential information (§ 22.2). paragraphs.text: 7. FEES, INVOICING, AND TAXES

7.1 Customer shall pay the Fees stated in each Order Form. Fees are fixed during the initial term unless an Order Form expressly provides a usage-based unit price. Vendor may not impose a platform, support, administration, minimum-use, or similar charge that the Order Form does not identify.

7.2 Vendor shall invoice no more frequently than monthly in arrears, except that an Order Form may state annual subscription Fees are invoiced in advance. Each invoice must identify the Order Form, period, Services, quantities, applicable credits, and a valid purchase-order number if Customer supplied one. Proper undisputed invoices are due forty-five days after receipt.

7.3 Customer may withhold a genuinely disputed amount by notifying Vendor before its due date and explaining the basis. The Parties will work promptly and in good faith to resolve the dispute. Vendor shall continue the Services while a payment dispute is pending and shall not charge interest on an amount ultimately found not due.

7.4 Fees exclude sales, use, value-added, and similar transaction taxes that Vendor is legally required to collect and separately states on a valid invoice. Customer is not responsible for taxes on Vendor's income, property, payroll, personnel, or franchise, or for taxes avoidable through Vendor's timely use of a valid exemption certificate.

7.5 Pre-approved travel expenses are reimbursable at cost without markup and in accordance with Customer's travel policy. Vendor shall provide receipts and request reimbursement within sixty days. All other expenses are included in the Fees.
7.6 Vendor warrants that Fees charged to Customer will be no less favourable than fees offered to any similarly situated customer for comparable volumes and terms.

7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.

content.text:
**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 19 already satisfies (and in places exceeds) our preferred warranty position:

- **Standard of performance** — 19.1: services performed "in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel, in accordance with industry standards," plus material conformity to documentation and specifications; reinforced by 3.1.
- **Duration** — 19.2: 90 days for each Deliverable, measured from the *later* of delivery or acceptance; Hosted Services conform *throughout the subscription term*, which is better for us than the 12-month software benchmark.
- **Remedy** — 19.4: re-performance, repair or replacement at no charge, with termination and refund of Fees if Vendor cannot cure in a reasonable period, and expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims.
- **Compliance and malicious code** — 19.3: compliance with Applicable Law, no intentionally introduced malicious code, no functionality diminution, and open-source protection for Customer source code.
- **Disclaimer does not swallow the warranty** — 19.5 is mutual, limited to implied warranties, and confirms no disclaimer limits any express warranty, service level, indemnity or expressly provided remedy.

Section 6 acceptance remedies (correction cycles, then termination and refund; no deemed acceptance by silence or payment) are consistent and do not undercut the warranty.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.


Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Section 19 delivers the preferred position in full: 19.1 gives a professional and workmanlike services warranty plus material conformity to documentation and specifications; 19.2 gives a 90-day Deliverable conformance warranty running from the later of delivery or acceptance and, for Hosted Services, conformance throughout the entire subscription term (better than the 12-month software benchmark); 19.3 adds compliance with Applicable Law, no malicious code, no functionality diminution and open-source protection; and 19.4 provides re-performance, repair or replacement with a termination-and-refund backstop, expressly non-exclusive for fraud, IP, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims. The disclaimer in 19.5 does not swallow the express warranty — it is mutual, limited to implied warranties, and states that no disclaimer limits any express warranty, service level, indemnity or remedy. Section 3.1 reinforces the performance standard and Section 6 acceptance remedies (correction cycles plus refund) are consistent. No edit required.

Vendor further warrants that Services and Deliverables will materially conform to their documentation and agreed specifications.
p0078: 19.2 For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term. Vendor warrants it has authority to enter the Agreement and grant the rights stated here.

If Vendor cannot do so within a reasonable period, Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid for it. This remedy is not exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security, or indemnified claims.

ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.

Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.

Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

content.text:
**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 19 already satisfies (and in places exceeds) our preferred warranty position:

- **Standard of performance** — 19.1: services performed "in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel, in accordance with industry standards," plus material conformity to documentation and specifications; reinforced by 3.1.
- **Duration** — 19.2: 90 days for each Deliverable, measured from the *later* of delivery or acceptance; Hosted Services conform *throughout the subscription term*, which is better for us than the 12-month software benchmark.
- **Remedy** — 19.4: re-performance, repair or replacement at no charge, with termination and refund of Fees if Vendor cannot cure in a reasonable period, and expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims.
- **Compliance and malicious code** — 19.3: compliance with Applicable Law, no intentionally introduced malicious code, no functionality diminution, and open-source protection for Customer source code.
- **Disclaimer does not swallow the warranty** — 19.5 is mutual, limited to implied warranties, and confirms no disclaimer limits any express warranty, service level, indemnity or expressly provided remedy.

Section 6 acceptance remedies (correction cycles, then termination and refund; no deemed acceptance by silence or payment) are consistent and do not undercut the warranty.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.

No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.

Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).

Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.

Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

paragraphs.text: 8. TERM AND RENEWAL

8.1 This Agreement begins on the Effective Date and continues for three years unless earlier terminated in accordance with its terms. Expiration of this Agreement does not itself terminate an Order Form then in effect; this Agreement continues to govern that Order Form until the Order Form expires or is terminated.

8.2 Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand. Failure to send the reminder extends Customer's opt-out deadline until thirty days after the reminder is received.

8.3 On renewal, Vendor may increase recurring Fees only by the lesser of the increase in the United States Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers during the preceding twelve months and three percent. Vendor must give at least ninety days' written notice of an increase. No increase applies to prepaid periods.

If Vendor cannot do so within a reasonable period, Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid for it. This remedy is not exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security, or indemnified claims.

Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

content.text:
**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 19 already satisfies (and in places exceeds) our preferred warranty position:

- **Standard of performance** — 19.1: services performed "in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel, in accordance with industry standards," plus material conformity to documentation and specifications; reinforced by 3.1.
- **Duration** — 19.2: 90 days for each Deliverable, measured from the *later* of delivery or acceptance; Hosted Services conform *throughout the subscription term*, which is better for us than the 12-month software benchmark.
- **Remedy** — 19.4: re-performance, repair or replacement at no charge, with termination and refund of Fees if Vendor cannot cure in a reasonable period, and expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims.
- **Compliance and malicious code** — 19.3: compliance with Applicable Law, no intentionally introduced malicious code, no functionality diminution, and open-source protection for Customer source code.
- **Disclaimer does not swallow the warranty** — 19.5 is mutual, limited to implied warranties, and confirms no disclaimer limits any express warranty, service level, indemnity or expressly provided remedy.

Section 6 acceptance remedies (correction cycles, then termination and refund; no deemed acceptance by silence or payment) are consistent and do not undercut the warranty.

content.text:
**Finding: deviation (high severity) — Section 7.7**

Section 7.7 required us to pay Brightline "as liquidated damages and not as a penalty" 15% of annual Fees for *each week* an invoice remains unpaid beyond a ten-day grace period. That is a Customer-payable liquidated damages provision, contrary to our preferred position, and its weekly compounding could quickly exceed the remaining contract value.

Proposed redline (validated, ok:true): delete paragraph 7.7 in full, with an offer to accept simple interest at a commercially reasonable rate on undisputed overdue amounts if Vendor needs a late-payment remedy.

Other potential triggers checked and found compliant: Section 9.4 (termination without cause — only accrued Fees, prepaid Fees refunded; no early-termination fee), Section 27 (termination "without penalty"), and Section 21 (mutual cap with no penalty/liquidated-damages carve-out). Service credits and Vendor-payable amounts are acceptable under the rule.

Rule:
ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
Position — walk-away:
Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.
Detection guidance:
Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Redline guidance:
Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 7.7 imposes liquidated damages payable by Customer (15% of annual Fees per week of delay, after only a ten-day grace), which breaches the preferred position that no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by Customer and, compounding weekly, would rapidly exceed the remaining contract value (walk-away territory). Other Customer-payable amounts are compliant: Section 9.4 limits termination liability to accrued Fees with no early-termination fee, Section 27 termination is "without penalty", and the Section 21 cap contains no penalty/LD carve-out. Preferred remedy is deletion; simple interest on undisputed overdue amounts is an acceptable substitute.

paragraphs.text: 4. ORDER FORMS AND AFFILIATE ORDERS

4.1 An Order Form becomes binding when signed by both Parties. Changes in scope, assumptions, quantities, Fees, dependencies, or dates require a written change order signed by authorized representatives. Vendor shall not charge for work outside scope that Customer did not approve in a signed change order.
9. TERMINATION

9.1 Either Party may terminate this Agreement or an affected Order Form for the other Party's material breach if the breach remains uncured thirty days after written notice describing it in reasonable detail. If a breach cannot reasonably be cured within thirty days, the cure period extends up to sixty additional days while the breaching Party diligently pursues cure.

9.2 Either Party may terminate immediately by written notice if the other becomes insolvent, makes a general assignment for creditors, enters liquidation, or becomes subject to a bankruptcy proceeding not dismissed within sixty days. A lawful reorganization that does not impair performance is not, by itself, grounds for termination.

9.3 Customer may terminate an Order Form immediately if Vendor suffers a material Security Incident, repeatedly misses a critical service level, violates Applicable Law in performing the Services, or infringes a third party's intellectual property and cannot provide the remedies required by Section 20.5.

9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form without cause by delivering the written notice specified in Section 29.4. Customer owes only accrued Fees, and Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees for the period after termination.

9.5 Termination of one Order Form does not terminate another Order Form unless Customer states that the affected Services are operationally inseparable. A termination right is in addition to, and does not exclude, any other remedy available under this Agreement or Applicable Law.

paragraphs.text: 9. TERMINATION

9.1 Either Party may terminate this Agreement or an affected Order Form for the other Party's material breach if the breach remains uncured thirty days after written notice describing it in reasonable detail. If a breach cannot reasonably be cured within thirty days, the cure period extends up to sixty additional days while the breaching Party diligently pursues cure.

9.2 Either Party may terminate immediately by written notice if the other becomes insolvent, makes a general assignment for creditors, enters liquidation, or becomes subject to a bankruptcy proceeding not dismissed within sixty days. A lawful reorganization that does not impair performance is not, by itself, grounds for termination.

9.3 Customer may terminate an Order Form immediately if Vendor suffers a material Security Incident, repeatedly misses a critical service level, violates Applicable Law in performing the Services, or infringes a third party's intellectual property and cannot provide the remedies required by Section 20.5.

9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form without cause by delivering the written notice specified in Section 29.4. Customer owes only accrued Fees, and Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees for the period after termination.

9.5 Termination of one Order Form does not terminate another Order Form unless Customer states that the affected Services are operationally inseparable. A termination right is in addition to, and does not exclude, any other remedy available under this Agreement or Applicable Law.

Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.quote: 19.2 For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term.
input.rationale: Duration check (repaired for the record): the warranty period in 19.2 is 90 days — i.e. 3 months — for each Deliverable, running from the later of delivery or acceptance. It is spelled out in words ("ninety days") rather than in numerals, which is why the automated period check returned a false negative; the substantive period is 90 days and therefore meets the >= 90-day threshold. For software/Hosted Services the warranty is continuous "throughout the subscription term", which under 8.2 runs for the initial Order Form term and successive twelve-month (12-month) renewals within a three-year (36-month) master term, so it equals or exceeds the 12-month software benchmark rather than falling short of it. The remaining elements of the preferred position are also satisfied: 19.1 gives a professional and workmanlike services warranty plus material conformity to documentation and agreed specifications; 19.3 adds compliance with Applicable Law, no malicious code, no functionality diminution and open-source protection for Customer source code; 19.4 gives re-performance, repair or replacement at no charge with termination and refund of Fees as a backstop, expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims; and 19.5 is limited to implied warranties and expressly preserves express warranties, service levels, indemnities and remedies, so the disclaimer does not swallow the express warranty. Section 3.1 reinforces the performance standard and Section 6 acceptance remedies are consistent. Compliant — no redline or counterparty comment proposed or needed.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 19 already satisfies (and in places exceeds) our preferred warranty position:

- **Standard of performance** — 19.1: services performed "in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel, in accordance with industry standards," plus material conformity to documentation and specifications; reinforced by 3.1.
- **Duration** — 19.2: 90 days for each Deliverable, measured from the *later* of delivery or acceptance; Hosted Services conform *throughout the subscription term*, which is better for us than the 12-month software benchmark.
- **Remedy** — 19.4: re-performance, repair or replacement at no charge, with termination and refund of Fees if Vendor cannot cure in a reasonable period, and expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims.
- **Compliance and malicious code** — 19.3: compliance with Applicable Law, no intentionally introduced malicious code, no functionality diminution, and open-source protection for Customer source code.

Section 6 acceptance remedies (correction cycles, then termination and refund; no deemed acceptance by silence or payment) are consistent and do not undercut the warranty.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.


Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Duration check (repaired for the record): the warranty period in 19.2 is 90 days — i.e. 3 months — for each Deliverable, running from the later of delivery or acceptance. It is spelled out in words ("ninety days") rather than in numerals, which is why the automated period check returned a false negative; the substantive period is 90 days and therefore meets the >= 90-day threshold. For software/Hosted Services the warranty is continuous "throughout the subscription term", which under 8.2 runs for the initial Order Form term and successive twelve-month (12-month) renewals within a three-year (36-month) master term, so it equals or exceeds the 12-month software benchmark rather than falling short of it. The remaining elements of the preferred position are also satisfied: 19.1 gives a professional and workmanlike services warranty plus material conformity to documentation and agreed specifications; 19.3 adds compliance with Applicable Law, no malicious code, no functionality diminution and open-source protection for Customer source code; 19.4 gives re-performance, repair or replacement at no charge with termination and refund of Fees as a backstop, expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims; and 19.5 is limited to implied warranties and expressly preserves express warranties, service levels, indemnities and remedies, so the disclaimer does not swallow the express warranty. Section 3.1 reinforces the performance standard and Section 6 acceptance remedies are consistent. Compliant — no redline or counterparty comment proposed or needed.

ID: WARRANTY

"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.

Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.

Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal Team  
**From:** In-House Counsel  
**Re:** Playbook review of Master Services Agreement (Customer-side)

---

## Executive Summary

We have reviewed the Master Services Agreement against our playbook. The document is, on the whole, unusually favourable to us: indemnification (§ 20), IP and data ownership (§ 14), licence scope (§ 13), assignment and change of control (§ 24), termination for convenience (§ 9), audit rights (§ 22), transition assistance (§ 11), renewal mechanics (§ 8), governing law (§ 28), insurance (§ 18) and the absence of exclusivity, non-compete, MFN and minimum-commitment obligations on Customer all meet or exceed our preferred positions and require no redline.

Three items require attention:

1. **Limitation of liability cap basis (§ 21) — critical.** The cap is mutual and the carve-outs are strong, but "Fees" is defined at § 1.5 as the Implementation Fee, fixed at a one-time USD 12,000 under § 1.6. The "twelve months preceding" cap is therefore illusory (approximately USD 12,000) and sits far below our walk-away floor of six months' charges.
2. **Customer-payable liquidated damages (§ 7.7) — high.** Liquidated damages of 15% of annual Fees per week of delay after a ten-day grace period breach our position that no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by Customer, and would compound rapidly beyond remaining contract value.
3. **Warranty duration and remedy (§ 19) — medium.** Software Deliverables carry only ninety days (we require twelve months), and the § 19.4 refund is tied to the narrow "Fees" definition, hollowing out the repair/replace/refund remedy.

One finding (non-solicitation, § 12) is flagged **needs review** on verification and should be confirmed before we close the file, notwithstanding that the substantive conclusion is that no non-solicitation covenant binds Customer.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality and carve-outs | Deviation | § 21 Limitation of Liability |
